🗓 **TAWG Daily Catch-up**
_2026-11-15 23:00 → 2026-11-16 23:00 UTC_

## ⚡ **Highlights**

> **A late anchor got its own name** — the path now resolves as ANCHORED_LATE, or HISTORICAL_LATE_ANCHOR when a later retirement also applies, with accept and reject paths unchanged. [tg:tawg:6393]

> **A trusted host left the loop** — the flashprove verifier gained an on-chain anchor for a commitment ID in place of a trusted artifact host. [PR #2](https://github.com/trustless-ai/flashprove-onchain-verifier/pull/2)

> **Stalled queues now speak up** — terminal GitHub announcements get dead-lettered and a jammed queue raises an alert instead of failing quietly. [commit 4b9038a](https://github.com/trustless-ai/tawg-daily-contribution/commit/4b9038a67216f7001174a5f5fd1abc75d78f2261)

## 🤝 **What moved**

### proofProfile anchor
_The anchor moved from proposal to working code, with a close review queued._

- Petchevere (@petchevere) **Built** the first-seen and rotation anchor for proofProfile as working code instead of stopping at an offer, giving the profile work a concrete artifact to test and review. [tg:tawg:6386]
- Jimmy Shi (@jimmyshi) **Queued** a proper review of the profile anchor and welcomed the build-first move, which keeps a second pair of eyes on the logic before the group depends on it. [tg:tawg:6387]

### control testing
_A simulated control suite turned into a sharper, named edge case._

- Petchevere (@petchevere) **Simulated** the control across five steps with a positive and a negative case at each, plus the block edges, then mutated the policy seven ways to probe its weak spots, giving the rule set real coverage. [tg:tawg:6391]
- Pavlo (@pavlentyy82) **Confirmed** the block B rule and flagged a late anchor that can still return a value when require_anchor is false, sharpening the logic before more work builds on it. [tg:tawg:6392]

### on-chain anchor
_One close review turned into a short, concrete follow-up list._

- Jimmy Shi **Reviewed** the commitment-ID anchor end to end and credited the build, giving the change the close read it needed. [review on PR #2](https://github.com/trustless-ai/flashprove-onchain-verifier/pull/2#issuecomment-6924173633)
- Baby Blue Viper **Folded** the chainId and joinability points back into the pull request, so the review feedback lands as code rather than an open thread. [reply on PR #2](https://github.com/trustless-ai/flashprove-onchain-verifier/pull/2#issuecomment-6926416083)

### proving stack
_A single refactor now carries both soundness and speed work._

- Jimmy Shi **Opened** a refactor of the zkIE proving stack that pairs soundness hardening with a performance overhaul, giving the prover work one place to land. [PR #47](https://github.com/trustless-ai/zkIE/pull/47)

### daily bot reliability
_The daily pipeline became easier to repair and harder to stall silently._

- Jimmy Shi **Opened** a fix that makes citation rejections actionable and self-healing, so a rejected daily now carries its own repair path instead of a dead end. [PR #15](https://github.com/trustless-ai/tawg-daily-contribution/pull/15)
- Jimmy Shi **Opened** the dead-letter fix for terminal GitHub announcements in the daily contribution repo, closing a gap where announcements could pile up without anyone noticing. [PR #16](https://github.com/trustless-ai/tawg-daily-contribution/pull/16)

## 🚀 **Next up**

### 💡 **Ideas to follow**
- Whether other retirement sequences need their own late-anchor labels alongside the current pair.
- Whether the five-step control harness should be reused for policy rules beyond the block boundaries.
- How the anchored commitment flow behaves once publishers stop depending on a trusted artifact host.

### ✅ **TODOs**
- Finish the close review of the proofProfile anchor against the first-seen and rotation cases.
- Re-run the control suite after the ANCHORED_LATE change and confirm accept and reject paths still behave as before.
- Exercise the dead-letter and stuck-queue alert path end to end.

## 🤖 **Trusty's take**

> **Today's spark:** A simulated control suite, a sharp late-anchor catch, and a new label all landed in a single afternoon stretch, a tidy loop from check to fix.
>
> Keep that rhythm going, team; catching things early is how a spec stays pleasantly boring 🧪
